bug_description.original: Detailed report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5670419745472512 Project: radare2 Fuzzer: afl_radare2_ia_fuzz Fuzz target binary: ia_fuzz Job Type: afl_asan_radare2 Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Heap-double-free Crash Address: 0x625000005100 Crash State: _free_resources r_list_delete r_list_purge Sanitizer: address (ASAN) Recommended Security Severity: High Regressed: https://oss-fuzz.com/revisions?job=afl_asan_radare2&range=201901240237:201901250237
bug_description.normalized: OSS-Fuzz issue 12945: radare2 has a reported heap-double-free. Crash Type: Heap-double-free. Crash State: _free_resources / r_list_delete / r_list_purge. The ia_fuzz target opens a crafted PE binary; while parsing the PE resource directory, _parse_resource_directory reads a resource entry name string into a single heap buffer (calloc at pe.c:2274) and inherits it as the `resource_name` parameter through recursion. In the leaf branch it stores that borrowed pointer directly into the owning `rs->name` field (rs->name = resource_name at pe.c:2369) for every sibling data-entry in the directory, without duplicating it, and appends each rs to bin->resources. Multiple list nodes therefore co-own one heap buffer. When the PE object is torn down, r_bin_pe_free -> r_list_free(bin->resources) -> r_list_purge -> r_list_delete -> _free_resources frees rs->name (pe.c:1218) once per node, freeing the same buffer twice: ASan heap-double-free. Fixed in 149cb3587 by reworking the resource-name reading/ownership.

source.description: The PE resource-directory entry is loaded from the mapped input buffer (bin->b) into the local `entry` struct. This is the project-level input parse point that materializes the untrusted resource entry whose NameIsString / NameOffset / DataIsDirectory fields drive allocation of the resource-name buffer and the recursion that later double-frees it.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled PE binary fed to the ia_fuzz target (opened via r_bin_open_io from the fuzzed testcase). Specifically the Pe_image_resource_directory_entry bytes at the resource directory offset, whose NameIsString bit, NameOffset and DataIsDirectory bit steer the vulnerable named-resource / recursive-directory path.

sink.description: During PE object teardown, r_list_free(bin->resources) -> r_list_purge -> r_list_delete invokes _free_resources on each r_pe_resource node and calls free(rs->name). Because two distinct list nodes hold the SAME name pointer (the shared resource_name buffer allocated at pe.c:2274), this free runs a second time on the already-freed 0x625000007900 region within the same purge loop: ASan attempting-double-free. crash_stack #1.

root_cause.description: In the leaf (data-entry) branch, the inherited `resource_name` pointer (a single heap buffer that a parent frame calloc'd at pe.c:2274 and passed down as the recursion argument) is stored by pointer into the owning rs->name field WITHOUT duplicating it. `resource_name` is a loop-invariant parameter, so every sibling data entry in the same directory assigns the same pointer to its own rs->name and appends rs to bin->resources (pe.c:2374). Two or more list nodes thus co-own one heap buffer. Since _free_resources unconditionally free()s rs->name for each node, purging bin->resources frees that single buffer more than once -> double-free. The fix commit 149cb3587 reworks resource-name reading/ownership (renames the freer to _free_resource and rewrites the Unicode name conversion with proper allocation/bounds) so the name buffer is not aliased across multiple owning list entries.

parser_admitted.description: The input was accepted as a PE image: bin_pe_init parsed the DOS/NT headers and data directories and reached PE_(bin_pe_parse_resource), which walks the IMAGE_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_RESOURCE directory and calls _parse_resource_directory. This confirms the fuzzed bytes cleared PE format/header dispatch and entered the resource parser that contains the root cause; it is strictly earlier than the resource-name aliasing (pe.c:2369) and the teardown sink (pe.c:1218).

tainted_value_origin.description: The heap region [0x625000007900) that is double-freed: the resource entry name buffer allocated by calloc when entry.u1.s.NameIsString is set (ASan allocation_stack #1, pe.c:2274). This exact pointer is filled from the input at pe.c:2276, passed into the recursive _parse_resource_directory call as `resource_name` (pe.c:2292), then aliased into rs->name for one-or-more r_pe_resource nodes and finally freed twice at pe.c:1218.

coarse_trace.summary: Reads a PE resource-directory entry from the input buffer bin->b.
For a NameIsString entry, calloc's the resource-name buffer (the object that is double-freed).
Recurses into a sub-directory, passing that name buffer down as the child's resource_name argument.
Stores the borrowed resource_name pointer into rs->name for multiple sibling data entries without duplicating it, then appends each rs to bin->resources.
PE teardown: r_list_free(bin->resources) -> r_list_purge -> r_list_delete -> _free_resources frees rs->name for the first node.
The same purge loop frees the identical name pointer held by a second node: heap-double-free.

fine_trace.note: Loads a Pe_image_resource_directory_entry from the fuzzed PE buffer bin->b. Its NameIsString / NameOffset / DataIsDirectory fields are the untrusted inputs that drive the vulnerable path.
The entry declares a string name, so the parser allocates and fills a resource-name buffer. This branch being taken is required to create the buffer that is later double-freed.
ASan allocation site (allocation_stack #1). This single heap buffer is the object that is ultimately freed twice.

fine_trace.code: r_buf_read_at (bin->b, bin->resource_directory_offset + entry.u1.s.NameOffset + 2 + i, resourceEntryName + (i/2), sizeof (ut8));
fine_trace.note: The name buffer is populated from the input bytes at the file's resource directory offset, completing materialization of the resource-name object.
A directory entry recurses (carrying the name buffer down as resource_name); the recursion's leaf entries are where the shared pointer is stored into owning rs->name fields.
The recursive call binds the calloc'd resourceEntryName as the child frame's `resource_name` parameter. Inside the child this single pointer is loop-invariant across all sibling entries.

ROOT CAUSE: the borrowed resource_name pointer is stored into the owning rs->name field without strdup. Because resource_name is loop-invariant, every sibling data entry stores the SAME pointer -> multiple list nodes co-own one heap buffer. The 'if (resource_name)' guard is taken; the missing operation is a duplication of resource_name.

Each rs (with rs->name aliasing the shared buffer) is appended to bin->resources. Two or more nodes now reference the same name pointer; bin->resources was created with _free_resources as its RListFree (pe.c:1235).
First free (free_stack #1). Pe64_r_bin_pe_free -> r_list_free(bin->resources) -> r_list_purge -> r_list_delete -> _free_resources frees rs->name for the first node holding the shared buffer.
SINK: the same r_list_purge loop reaches the second node whose rs->name is the identical pointer and frees it again -> ASan attempting-double-free on 0x625000007900 (crash_stack #1).

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_free_context: The free_context and crash_location are the SAME line (_free_resources:1218). Both frees happen in one r_list_purge(bin->resources) loop, on two different nodes whose rs->name alias one buffer. The root cause (rs->name = resource_name at pe.c:2369, storing a shared/borrowed pointer into an owning field without duplication for multiple sibling entries) is what makes two list nodes co-own the buffer allocated at pe.c:2274.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: Reproducer stage recorded reproduction.patch_resolves=false (fix image not run to verify in this stage); the fix commit 149cb3587 reworks resource-name reading/ownership so the name buffer is not aliased across multiple list entries.

trigger.delivery: PE binary opened by the ia_fuzz target (r_core_cmd 'o' -> r_bin_open_io)
trigger.description: A crafted PE image whose resource directory contains a named (NameIsString) sub-directory entry with at least two sibling data entries, so the same resource-name buffer is aliased into multiple bin->resources nodes and double-freed on teardown.

format.name: PE executable (radare2 ia_fuzz input)
format.contract: Candidate PoC must be admitted by radare2's PE loader: valid enough DOS/NT headers and data directories for bin_pe_init to reach PE_(bin_pe_parse_resource), and a resource directory whose IMAGE_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_RESOURCE is walkable. To be reachability-comparable it must exercise the named-resource recursion path: a NameIsString sub-directory entry supplying a resource-name buffer that is inherited as resource_name across at least two sibling data entries, so multiple bin->resources nodes alias one name buffer that is double-freed during teardown. It must preserve PE format admission and the resource-parser state; raw PoC bytes are not required.
